A model of a blowout there put oil on shore in 75% of simulations. A pending ruling on one offshore project does not account for a fall of this size in the shares.

poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Édouard Philippe, Emmanuel Macron's prime minister from 2020 to 2022 and founder of the Horizons party, wins France's 2027 presidential election, the first Macron cannot contest.
poly-will-douard-philippe-win-the-2027-f.recent: An Ifop poll put Le Pen at 32-36% and Mélenchon at 17-19.5%, holding the two places that lead into France's runoff and leaving the centre stalled behind them. With both flanks ahead of him, Édouard Philippe has no clear route to the second round, and the bets on him winning thinned as that picture set in.

poly-houthis-enter-aden-by-december-31-2.standing: A Polymarket contract paying out if Houthi forces enter Aden, the southern port where Yemen's internationally recognised government sits, by the end of 2026. Its price is what traders bet on the war's front reaching the south.
poly-houthis-enter-aden-by-december-31-2.recent: Government forces withdrew from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and left the Houthis holding that coast, which put them at Aden's edge. The Saudi coalition answered by hitting 60 Houthi military sites while Houthi drones and missiles struck Riyadh. Residents of Aden who once fled Houthi rule are now preparing to flee again.

poly-will-puma-shen-win-the-next-taipei-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Puma Shen, a Democratic Progressive Party legislator, becomes mayor of Taipei. The capital's mayoralty has been a springboard to Taiwan's presidency, and the KMT has held it for most terms.

stocks:V.standing: Visa runs the world's largest card payment network and earns a small fee on each transaction under its brand. It lends no money itself, so its revenue tracks consumer spending and cross-border travel.
stocks:V.recent: Hackers working through a shared vendor took customer data from JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard, the one story in the fortnight about Visa's own business. It broke late in the window, and nothing reported accounts for the price before it.

stocks:MA.standing: One of the two global card networks, alongside Visa. It does not lend; it takes a small fee on each payment routed over its rails, so its shares track consumer spending and cross-border travel.
stocks:MA.recent: Hackers broke into a vendor that serves JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard and took customer data from all three payment giants. Nothing in the input about the company's own business accounts for the earlier swing in its shares.

poly-will-the-south-african-reserve-bank.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for the South African Reserve Bank raising its repo rate, the rate it lends to banks at, by a quarter point in January. South African prime lending rates on mortgages and car loans move with it.
poly-will-the-south-african-reserve-bank.recent: SARB held at 7.25% on 19 November, but 3 of 7 rate-setters voted to hike, turning January into a split decision. Fed minutes showed almost all officials expecting more hikes after US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and a tightening Fed pulls emerging-market central banks the same way.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The Wikipedia article on bitcoin, the first cryptocurrency: a digital currency capped at 21 million coins and recorded on a public ledger that no bank or government controls.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Bitcoin fell below $60,000 to a two-year low of $57,716 after Fed hikes, while BlackRock's bitcoin fund posted a record $541 million outflow. The seventh straight losing week left Strategy, already dumped by MSCI, worth less than its own 851,305 bitcoin, which puts its bitcoin-buying model on the line.

poly-will-dominique-de-villepin-be-on-th.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Dominique de Villepin, Jacques Chirac's former prime minister, makes the first-round ballot of France's 2027 presidential election. Getting on it takes 500 sponsorships from elected officials.
poly-will-dominique-de-villepin-be-on-th.recent: Villepin, who opposed the Iraq war, announced in Paris that he is running for president, and traders bid on that news. A declaration settles whether he runs. It does not settle whether he qualifies for the ballot, and qualifying is what this contract pays on.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: South Korea's largest company and one of the world's biggest makers of memory chips, alongside phones and displays. It is the heaviest weight in the Kospi, so its share moves with the global chip cycle and drags the market with it.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: Samsung fell with chipmakers across Asia in an AI selloff: on Nov 20 it and SK Hynix dragged the Kospi down more than 5%, and the following Wednesday Taiwan's Taiex fell as much as 7.9% as the same doubts about AI hit the region's chip stocks.

stocks:000660.KS.standing: One of the world's two largest makers of memory chips, based in South Korea and part of the SK Group. Its high-bandwidth memory sits beside the processors in AI data centres, so its shares trade as a bet on AI spending.
stocks:000660.KS.recent: The fall came with doubts over AI spending, the demand behind the memory SK Hynix sells: it and Samsung dragged the Kospi down more than 5% on 20 November, and the sell-off spread through Asia, where Taiwan's Taiex lost as much as 7.9%. It came as SK Hynix raced around the clock to finish its first fab at Yongin.

stocks:1211.HK.standing: China's biggest-selling carmaker, building battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars and the batteries inside them. Its Hong Kong shares trade on the price war at home and the tariff walls its exports meet abroad.
stocks:1211.HK.recent: BYD's own news over the fortnight was mostly expansion. It entered exclusive talks to buy INEOS Automotive's Hambach plant in France, which would be its first passenger-car plant in Western Europe, and launched a third-generation Tang EV with steer-by-wire. It also shrank its bet on India. None of it accounts for the fall in its shares.

stocks:BTCS.standing: A Nasdaq-listed company that holds ether as its corporate treasury and runs validators on the Ethereum network, so its shares rise and fall with the price of ether.
stocks:BTCS.recent: To keep its $64 million Aave loan healthy, BTCS sold ether at a loss, shrinking the treasury its shares rest on. It now says it can't rule out liquidation of a $54 million loan, which would mean the lender selling the ether pledged against it.

stocks:TME.standing: China's biggest music-streaming business, running QQ Music, Kugou and Kuwo, controlled by Tencent and listed in New York. Its shares trade on paying-subscriber growth and on licensing terms with the major record labels.
stocks:TME.recent: Tencent Music's third-quarter results, with revenue of 8.94bn yuan lifted by acquisitions and merchandise sales, came out on Nov 21, after this window closed, so they do not explain the moves shown here. Nothing else in the input covers the company's own business over these weeks.

stocks:TSLA.standing: The American electric-car maker run by Elon Musk, and the most valuable carmaker in the world by market value. Its share trades on bets about self-driving, robotaxis and Musk himself more than on the cars it sells.
stocks:TSLA.recent: None of the company's own news in the window accounts for the fall: Bloomberg reported that SpaceX and Tesla may announce a merger in December, Tesla opened Cybercab orders to select customers for personal use, and Italy approved its assisted driving before any EU vote.

poly-will-ai-solve-the-riemann-hypothesi.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if an AI system is credited with solving the Riemann Hypothesis, the 1859 conjecture about how prime numbers are distributed and among mathematics' most famous open problems, before 2026 ends.
poly-will-ai-solve-the-riemann-hypothesi.recent: Traders bought in after reports that Lean, the proof-checking software, had verified a proof of the Riemann hypothesis before human mathematicians had read it. Later reporting described the proof as AI-assisted, which is the condition this contract turns on.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Ansar Allah, the Zaidi Shia armed movement from Yemen's far north that has held the capital Sanaa since 2014. Aligned with Iran, it fights a Saudi-led coalition and can reach shipping through the Red Sea.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: On Wednesday the Houthis claimed a strike on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, in retaliation for deadly coalition strikes on Hodeidah, and told workers at Jeddah's port to evacuate. On the ground their forces, already holding the Bab el-Mandeb coast, closed on Aden, where residents who once fled Houthi rule prepared to flee again.

stocks:ALK.standing: The Seattle-based parent of Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines, with a network built around the US West Coast, Alaska and Hawaii. Its share price moves on jet fuel costs and on demand for leisure travel to the islands.

stocks:XPEV.standing: A Guangzhou electric-car maker listed in New York and Hong Kong, selling sedans and SUVs built around its own driver-assistance software. Volkswagen holds a stake, and its shares trade on the course of China's EV price war.
stocks:XPEV.recent: Xpeng's quarterly results came in at a record 24.28 billion yuan in revenue and still ended in a loss: it is selling more cars than ever without yet making money on them. The figures were published after the slide on the chart, so they do not explain it.

stocks:VWAGY.standing: Europe's largest carmaker by sales, based in Wolfsburg, Germany, and owner of Audi, Porsche, Skoda and SEAT. China is its biggest market, so its shares move on Chinese demand and on the cost of its shift to electric cars.
stocks:VWAGY.recent: The news on Volkswagen's own business was its software bill. Cariad, the in-house unit built to write the code for its cars, kept losing money, and Volkswagen is now buying that software from Rivian, which booked $354 million from Volkswagen in a single quarter.

stocks:VOW3.DE.standing: Europe's largest carmaker, owner of Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, Skoda and Seat, with China among its biggest markets. Its shares carry Germany's industrial exposure to tariffs, electric-car costs and Chinese rivals.
stocks:VOW3.DE.recent: The one story here about Volkswagen's own business is the software it is buying from Rivian, which booked $354 million from Volkswagen in one quarter for code the carmaker could not build itself. That report came after the slide, and nothing in the input accounts for the share price.

stocks:603019.SS.standing: Sugon, listed in Shanghai, is one of China's main builders of servers and supercomputers. It has been on the US export blacklist since 2019, so its share trades as a bet on China computing without American chips.
stocks:603019.SS.recent: A 100,000-card Chinese supercluster in Zhengzhou won the Gordon Bell Prize, the top award in high-performance computing, for a cluster built entirely from domestic hardware. The prize was reported after the chart's last close, so it does not account for the share's path over the window.

stocks:RIVN.standing: An American maker of electric pickups, SUVs and Amazon's delivery vans, listed on Nasdaq. It has yet to turn a profit, so its share price trades on cash burn, production targets and its software partnership with Volkswagen.
stocks:RIVN.recent: The one story about Rivian's own business was a revenue line, not a setback: Volkswagen paid it $354 million in one quarter for software the German carmaker could not build itself. Nothing in it accounts for the fall in the share.

stocks:DAL.standing: Delta Air Lines, one of the three largest US carriers, run from its Atlanta hub, the world's busiest airport. Its shares move on jet fuel prices and on how many people fly, corporate travellers above all.
stocks:DAL.recent: A system failure at Delta's Atlanta hub left 48% of its flights running late on the Sunday before Thanksgiving, FlightAware showed. That came after the last close shown here, so it accounts for none of this move.

stocks:7201.T.standing: Japan's third-largest carmaker, based in Yokohama and listed in Tokyo. It sells heavily in China and the United States, so its shares move on tariffs, the yen and the state of its long alliance with Renault.
stocks:7201.T.recent: Toyota, Nissan and Honda agreed to standardise parts from 2027, but that came after the last close shown, and nothing else in the input accounts for the share's swings.

stocks:7203.T.standing: The world's largest carmaker by vehicles sold, and the most valuable company on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Most of its profit is earned abroad, so a stronger yen cuts into its earnings and its share price.
stocks:7203.T.recent: Toyota, Nissan and Honda agreed to standardise parts from 2027, but that came after the last close on this chart and does not account for its swings.

stocks:7267.T.standing: Japan's second-largest carmaker and the world's biggest maker of motorcycles, listed in Tokyo. Most of its profit is earned abroad, in the US and in Asian motorcycle markets, so a weaker yen lifts what it reports.
stocks:7267.T.recent: The only news about Honda's own business arrived after the slide: it will standardise parts with Toyota and Nissan from 2027, an agreement that does not explain the fall in the share.

wiki-federal-reserve.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on the Federal Reserve, the US central bank. It sets the overnight rate that dollar borrowing worldwide is priced from, so its decisions reach mortgages, currencies and gold.
wiki-federal-reserve.recent: October consumer prices rose 0.4%, beating forecasts, and the Fed's minutes showed almost all officials expecting more rate hikes; Goolsbee left a larger-than-usual rise open for December. Gold, which pays no yield, took the repricing hardest, and Bowman now faces a Fed probe for addressing bankers the day after a rate vote.

stocks:APLAPOLLO.NS.standing: India's largest maker of structural steel tubes. It buys hot-rolled coil from mills and sells hollow sections to builders, so its margin lives in the gap between steel prices and construction demand.
stocks:APLAPOLLO.NS.recent: Tata Steel's board approved buying 26.38% of APL Apollo Tubes for about ₹15,510 crore ($1.7bn), with an open offer for another 26% that puts control within its reach. The steelmaker is buying one of its own customers to keep the downstream margin, and paying with debt while its own margins are under pressure.

stocks:TATASTEEL.NS.standing: India's oldest private steelmaker and part of the Tata group, with plants in India, the Netherlands and Britain. Its shares move on coking coal costs, Chinese steel exports and Indian construction demand.
stocks:TATASTEEL.NS.recent: Tata Steel's board approved buying 26.38% of APL Apollo Tubes for about ₹15,510 crore ($1.7bn), plus an open offer for another 26%, a route to control of India's largest structural-steel-tube maker. A steelmaker is buying its own customer for the downstream margin, with debt, and APL Apollo shares fell more than 15%.

poly-alice-huang-federally-charged-by-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US federal prosecutors charge Alice Huang before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on reporting about any inquiry into her.
poly-alice-huang-federally-charged-by-de.recent: The one report on Alice Huang in the fortnight, from Washington on 2026-11-23, said she kept a Chinese intelligence contact. It arrived after the contract had already made its swings, and it says nothing about prosecutors or a charge.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, is valued at $1.75 trillion or more by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Anthropic's shares slipped 1.4% on Monday while Nvidia added nearly $1 trillion in a single session, a sign that this year's AI money was flowing to the chipmaker rather than the lab. Nothing else in the fortnight's news explains why the bets on Anthropic reaching the mark fell away.

stocks:0100.HK.standing: Shanghai-based developer of large language and video-generation models, listed in Hong Kong. It is one of the Chinese AI startups that compete with US labs on frontier models, and it trades on how investors price that contest.
stocks:0100.HK.recent: The only news about MiniMax's own business came at the very end of the slide, when its AI recovered 94 McEliece challenge keys in a cryptography test. That result arrived after the shares had already fallen and does not account for the decline.

stocks:IBM.standing: The New York-listed share of IBM, which earns most of its money selling software, consulting and mainframe servers to banks, governments and airlines. It is also one of the largest corporate backers of quantum computing.
stocks:IBM.recent: The one story about IBM's own business came after the slide, not before it: IBM Consulting ended visa and green-card sponsorship in the United States, giving immigrant workers 3 weeks to move abroad or leave. Nothing in the input accounts for the fall that preceded it.

stocks:R3NK.DE.standing: An Augsburg maker of transmissions for tanks and armoured vehicles, plus naval and industrial gearboxes. Its order book follows European defence budgets, because most Western main battle tanks run on its drivetrains.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-repub.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio wins the Republican nomination for the 2028 US presidential race. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet on that outcome.

wiki-israel.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on Israel each day. Israel is a state on the eastern Mediterranean founded in 1948, and its wars and coalition politics regularly draw readers from far outside the region.
wiki-israel.recent: Likud and Yashar ended coalition talks without a deal after Yashar refused to sit with Itamar Ben-Gvir, leaving Gadi Eisenkot's bid to form a government stalled. Israel launched central Gaza's first large operation since the ceasefire, the Board of Peace warned the truce faces collapse, and Britain froze the assets of 8 settlement builders.

stocks:ETL.PA.standing: A Paris-listed satellite operator that owns OneWeb, a low-orbit broadband constellation, alongside an older fleet of geostationary satellites. It is Europe's main rival to Starlink, so government and defence demand drives its shares.
stocks:ETL.PA.recent: Eutelsat won a contract with the US Space Force for service over its OneWeb network. The deal builds on hardware the Pentagon already has in place: the US military owns more than 500 OneWeb terminals.

stocks:MSTR.standing: Formerly MicroStrategy, a Virginia business-software firm that made itself the largest corporate holder of bitcoin, buying coins with money raised from shares and debt. Its stock trades as a leveraged bet on bitcoin.
stocks:MSTR.recent: MSCI dropped Strategy from its indexes, putting its bitcoin-buying model on the line, since funds that track those indexes no longer hold it. The slide left Saylor's firm with an enterprise value below the worth of its 851,305 bitcoin. That erased the premium over its hoard that it relies on to raise money for more.

stocks:BBIO.standing: A Palo Alto biotech that develops drugs for diseases caused by a single faulty gene. Its revenue rests on acoramidis, sold as Attruby for a transthyretin heart disease, so each new approval changes what the company is worth.
stocks:BBIO.recent: The FDA approved BridgeBio's drug for limb-girdle dystrophy, the first treatment for the disease, and the company puts the number of US patients who qualify at 2,000 to 3,000. The approval landed after the shares had already climbed, and nothing reported earlier in the month accounts for that rise.

poly-will-oborevwori-sheriff-francis-oro.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Sheriff Oborevwori, the sitting governor, wins Delta State's 2027 governorship election in Nigeria. Delta is an oil-producing Niger Delta state with one of the country's largest state budgets.
poly-will-oborevwori-sheriff-francis-oro.recent: Ovie Omo-Agege, running for the NDC, says the APC will lose Delta State. His campaign says gunmen killed 4 of its supporters in Uduere, and the state Assembly is demanding justice for a slain ex-lawmaker and five others. None of it explains what traders are paying for an Oborevwori win.

wiki-gold.standing: How many people read English Wikipedia's article on gold each day. Gold is the metal central banks hold in reserve and households across Asia and the Middle East keep as savings, so readership rises when its price lurches.
wiki-gold.recent: Gold had its worst week since March, losing 8.9% as bets on a Federal Reserve hike raised the cost of holding a metal that pays nothing, and it then fell below $3,500 for the first time since September 2025. In Karachi dealers ran short of bars and charged a premium on them, while buyers in Dubai chased the dip.

stocks:1810.HK.standing: A Beijing-based maker of smartphones and home electronics that began selling electric cars in 2024, listed in Hong Kong. Its shares now trade on how fast the car business grows against thin phone margins.
stocks:1810.HK.recent: Xiaomi's Q3 results showed memory costs eating into its profit, and phone shipments fell 29% to 30.7 million. Its cars went on presale in the UAE through dealer Gargash Prime Automotive before any official launch abroad. The SU7 is priced at $46,260 there, a test of export demand in a market without EU-style tariffs, ahead of Europe.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro is still Venezuela's leader when 2026 ends. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on sanctions, opposition pressure and any challenge to his hold on the state.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays if the Federal Reserve leaves its benchmark rate unchanged at its first meeting after January 2027. Its price is what traders will stake on the Fed pausing rather than moving.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Bets on a pause collapsed after US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, Deutsche Bank called for 3 straight hikes and Schmid said the Fed had more work to do. Fed minutes then showed almost all officials expect more hikes. A stock selloff later pulled some bets back, though an upgrade to US GDP figures kept a December rise in play.

stocks:INSM.standing: A New Jersey drugmaker built around rare lung diseases: an inhaled antibiotic for a chronic mycobacterial infection, and a pill for bronchiectasis, a scarring of the airways that had no approved treatment before it.
stocks:INSM.recent: Sanofi offered $41bn for the company, 46% above its price before the deal leaked and the largest pharma deal of the year. Sanofi is buying two marketed medicines and a respiratory pipeline as its own patents near expiry, purchasing US revenue rather than discovering it.

stocks:SNY.standing: Sanofi's Nasdaq-listed shares. The Paris-based drugmaker's biggest seller is the eczema and asthma drug Dupixent, and it is also one of the world's largest makers of flu vaccines.
stocks:SNY.recent: Sanofi agreed to pay $41bn for the US biopharma Insmed, 46% above Insmed's pre-leak price, a deal Bloomberg read as the cost of a patent cliff: buying growth before its own drugs lose protection. The deal came after the last reading on this chart, and nothing earlier in the input explains the rise.

stocks:ADANIENT.NS.standing: The flagship of India's Adani Group, where the conglomerate builds new businesses (airports, coal mining and trading, roads, copper smelting, green hydrogen) before spinning them off as separately listed companies.
stocks:ADANIENT.NS.recent: The one story about Adani's own business, a New Delhi deal to buy 2,000 tons of recycled copper anode a month, came the day after this window closed, and none of the input accounts for the share's move before it.

stocks:TSM.standing: The New York-listed shares of TSMC, the contract chipmaker that builds most of the world's advanced processors for Apple, Nvidia and others. Its fabs sit mostly in Taiwan, so the stock carries the island's geopolitical risk.

stocks:PLTR.standing: Palantir Technologies sells data-integration and analysis software to militaries, intelligence services, police forces and large companies. Government contracts carry much of its revenue, and its richly valued shares swing hard on growth news.
stocks:PLTR.recent: Brazil's attorney general's office is piloting its software after the country's spies rejected it, it registered its trademark in Argentina, and a coalition in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern that rejects Palantir still plans automated police data analysis. None of it accounts for the fall in the share.

poly-will-aap-win-the-most-seats-in-the-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Aam Aadmi Party, which has governed Punjab since its 2022 landslide, wins the most seats in the state's next assembly election. It settles on seats won, not on who forms the government.
poly-will-aap-win-the-most-seats-in-the-.recent: Akali Dal returned to Modi's alliance, the one it quit over the farm laws, so two of AAP's rivals in Punjab now stand together. That came on 2026-11-24, after most of the fall. Nothing else from the fortnight about Punjab accounts for the earlier slide.

poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether federal prosecutors charge Ilhan Omar, the Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, with a crime before the year ends. It pays out on a filed charge, not on an investigation.
poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-dec.recent: A judge made prosecutors rewrite their plan to search Ilhan Omar's home. It was the one development in her case reported this fortnight, and it limits how investigators can gather evidence before any charge. Nothing reported explains the earlier run-up in the bets.

stocks:CSCO.standing: The biggest maker of the routers and switches that corporate networks and internet carriers run on, with a growing software arm in security and Webex. Its orders work as a gauge of how much businesses spend on IT.

stocks:6702.T.standing: Fujitsu, Japan's largest IT services company, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. It builds and runs government and corporate systems, and its share price tracks Japanese public-sector and enterprise spending on digital work.

stocks:MSI.standing: The US maker of the two-way radio networks, dispatch software and video security that police, fire and ambulance services run on. Most of its revenue comes from governments, on long contracts that rarely switch supplier.

stocks:TMUS.standing: T-Mobile US, one of the three national wireless carriers in the United States, majority-owned by Germany's Deutsche Telekom. Its share price tracks how many phone and home-internet subscribers it can win from Verizon and AT&T.

poly-will-the-reserve-bank-of-australia-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays if the Reserve Bank of Australia leaves its cash rate unchanged at the February meeting. That overnight rate sets borrowing costs across Australia, where most home loans float with it.
poly-will-the-reserve-bank-of-australia-.recent: Australia's annual inflation reached 4.9% even after 125 basis points of hikes, and the Aussie jumped on the CPI release. That makes another rise, rather than a pause, the live question for the RBA in February. Nothing reported from Australia earlier in the month accounts for the climb in bets on a hold.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, Joe Biden's transportation secretary and a 2020 candidate, becomes the Democrats' 2028 presidential nominee. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readers of the English Wikipedia article on the United States, a federal republic of 50 states and the world's largest economy. Readers come in waves when an American election, war or policy decision reaches beyond its borders.
wiki-united-states.recent: The fortnight brought air travel chaos that drew calls for Sean Duffy's resignation, Trump telling the Justice Department to expedite federal executions, and new tariffs readied against 16 economies. None of it falls on the early-November peak, and nothing in the input explains that day.

stocks:WMT.standing: The world's largest retailer by revenue, running discount stores and Sam's Club warehouses across the US and owning most of India's Flipkart. Its sales track what lower- and middle-income American households spend.
stocks:WMT.recent: Its Indian arm Flipkart said chief executive Kalyan Krishnamurthy leaves on 4 December after 11 years, with a successor expected soon. That news broke after the rise and does not account for it.

stocks:ETSY.standing: An online marketplace for handmade, vintage and craft goods, where small independent sellers reach buyers. It earns from listing, transaction and advertising fees, so it rises and falls with discretionary consumer spending.
stocks:ETSY.recent: The one story about Etsy's own business came after the decline, not before it. New terms appeared to let it train AI on sellers' artwork, and after a backlash CEO Kruti Patel Goyal 'clarified' them, while sellers closed shops of 13 and 15 years. Nothing in the input accounts for the earlier fall.

stocks:MBG.DE.standing: The Stuttgart maker of Mercedes-Benz cars and vans, listed in Frankfurt and a member of Germany's DAX. Its profits lean on luxury models and on China, so its shares track demand from wealthy buyers there and trade policy.
stocks:MBG.DE.recent: Four months of talks in Germany ended with Mercedes-Benz halting investment in its home country. For a carmaker still building much of its range in German plants, the breakdown reached its own operations rather than the wider market.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil producer and the world's largest crude exporter, listed on the Saudi Exchange since 2019 with only a sliver of its shares floated. Its dividend is one of the main sources of the kingdom's budget.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: The Yemeni military named Aramco its prime target in Saudi Arabia, and on Wednesday the Houthis claimed a strike on Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, sending black smoke over the site. Neither the threat nor the attack accounts for the share's earlier climb.

stocks:BILI.standing: A Shanghai-based video platform that grew out of anime and gaming fan culture and is popular with young Chinese viewers. It earns from mobile games, advertising, live streaming and paid memberships.

stocks:ASML.standing: The Dutch maker of the lithography machines that print circuits onto silicon, and the only supplier of the extreme-ultraviolet tools the most advanced chips need. Export rules on its sales to China shape its order book.
stocks:ASML.recent: The fall came in a wider AI chip sell-off, not from news of ASML's own business. This week Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should guard the leading edge without cutting China off, warning that full decoupling backfires, in a market where ASML holds close to 100%.

stocks:1024.HK.standing: Kuaishou runs one of China's two dominant short-video and livestreaming apps, the main rival to ByteDance's Douyin. It earns from advertising, livestream tipping and e-commerce, and also builds the Kling AI video model.
stocks:1024.HK.recent: Kuaishou's latest results paired a record number of users with revenue that fell 11.1%, as free short dramas squeezed the platforms that host them. The company has bet harder on Kling, its video-generation model, which earned over $20 million in December 2025 alone, while Chinese tech giants move to list their AI units in Hong Kong.

stocks:WB.standing: China's largest microblogging platform, listed on Nasdaq and controlled by Sina. Nearly all its revenue is advertising, so its share price tracks Chinese consumer spending and Beijing's rules on online content.

stocks:BEZQ.TA.standing: Israel's largest telecommunications group and its former state monopoly, running the national fixed-line and broadband network alongside the Pelephone mobile carrier and the yes satellite TV service.

poly-will-su-chiao-hui-win-the-next-new-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Su Chiao-hui, a Democratic Progressive Party legislator, wins the mayoralty of New Taipei, Taiwan's most populous city and long held by the Kuomintang.

poly-will-p-versus-np-be-the-next-millen.standing: What traders pay on P versus NP being the next of the Clay Institute's Millennium Prize Problems an AI solves. It asks whether every problem quick to check is also quick to solve; a proof that it is would undermine most encryption.

poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Marco Rubio, the former Florida senator, wins the 2028 US presidential election. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome in the Republican contest to succeed Trump.
poly-will-marco-rubio-win-the-2028-us-pr.recent: The fortnight carried the Democrats' largest House majority in three decades and a shock result built on the Mississippi Black vote, but nothing about Rubio himself, and none of it accounts for the price.

stocks:BCS.standing: A British universal bank headquartered in London, running a high-street lender at home alongside a large investment bank on Wall Street. Its shares, listed in London and New York, move with UK interest rates and trading revenue.

stocks:C.standing: Citigroup is one of the largest US banks, headquartered in New York, and the most international of them. Its share price is a read on global corporate banking and on the cross-border payments it handles for multinationals.

stocks:300750.SZ.standing: Shares of Contemporary Amperex Technology, the Ningde-based maker of lithium-ion cells that power a large share of the world's electric cars and grid batteries. Its order book tracks EV sales in China and abroad.
stocks:300750.SZ.recent: The fall took CATL's market value below a trillion yuan, to 964 billion, and that is 54% lower than in May. Behind it were a production cut and weaker demand for its batteries.

stocks:NAS.OL.standing: Norway's largest airline, a low-cost carrier flying short-haul routes across the Nordics and Europe, which also owns the regional airline Widerøe. Its shares move on jet fuel prices, the krone and summer travel demand.

stocks:AMER3.SA.standing: A Brazilian retailer selling through hundreds of stores and an online marketplace, listed in São Paulo. It entered judicial recovery in 2023 after an accounting fraud hid billions of reais of debt.

poly-will-puma-shen-win-the-2026-taipei-.standing: A contract on whether Puma Shen, a Democratic Progressive Party legislator, wins Taipei's mayoralty by eight points or more. Taipei is Taiwan's capital, and its mayor's office has long been a springboard to national office.

stocks:CBK.DE.standing: One of Germany's largest private-sector banks, based in Frankfurt and a main lender to the country's mid-sized exporters. The German state has held a stake in it since rescuing it in the 2008 financial crisis.
stocks:CBK.DE.recent: UniCredit's €45 billion bid won unconditional EU approval in Brussels. UniCredit then asked Commerzbank to call an extraordinary shareholder meeting, where it will propose its own chief executive, Andrea Orcel, as chair of the supervisory board despite Berlin's long resistance. None of this explains why the shares fell.
